title: Determinism and numerical reproducibility
subtitle: Bit-identical or nothing, wherever the reference is bitwise with itself.

of 484 ranked lists matched against an independent implementation

lede: A rewrite or a kernel patch that changes one output bit invalidates every parity result above it, so I made bit-for-bit reproducibility ActiveKV's release standard. The exact BF16 path passes only when its output is bit-identical to fully resident attention. To make that reachable, I had the paged-attention kernel patched to emit its log-sum-exp statistic, so attention computed over on-card and host-resident history merges exactly. For parity runs, a validation switch makes the variable 4-bit GEMM reductions deterministic, and the release build is bit-identical to it with the switch off. I wrote the parity doctrine, and its first rule is that I run the reference twice before trusting a bitwise gate.
quote: A non-deterministic baseline fails against itself.
evidence: Numerical reproducibility and bitwise validation: a Python-to-C++ port that matched 13 of 13 exact cells and 12 of 12 compressed cells bitwise.
Deterministic GPU computation: a batched CUDA decoder identical across shuffled batch compositions in 2,345 of 2,345 rank-one checks, 484 of 484 ranked lists matched.
Reproducible ML pipelines: NVFP4 quantisation in about 15 seconds, byte-identical on re-run, so a rebuilt model can be compared with the one it replaces.
author: Corey James
